1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



As a Staff Security Engineer on Security Incident Response, you'll serve as a senior technical leader and builder for the team, helping shape both how we respond to incidents today and how our response capabilities evolve over time.This role is about advancing what the team is capable of, not just responding when something breaks. You'll design and build the AI-assisted systems that extend the team's reach, lead the response to the most complex incidents, and own programs that make the organization more prepared over time, from tabletop exercises and gamedays to the continued advancement of threat hunting and insider risk capabilities.



You bring engineering depth, sound incident judgment, and the ability to plan, and deliver complex work against a longer-term maturity roadmap not just execute against a queue.



This is a senior individual contributor role with organization-wide impact on how 1Password investigates, contains, and learns from security incidents.



This role reports to the Manager, Security Incident Response.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

 - Significant experience leading complex, high-severity security incidents across multiple environments, including serving as an incident commander or equivalent technical lead.

 - Experience designing and building AI-assisted or agentic automation for security operations (triage, investigation, containment), with sound judgment about where automation should and shouldn't hold decision authority.

 - Strong software engineering skills, and experience building production tooling, automation, or systems rather than only operating existing security platforms.

 - Experience owning a security program or capability roadmap end to end, including planning, sequencing, and delivering multi-quarter work.

 - Strong understanding of cloud-native, SaaS, and identity-driven attack techniques and response approaches.

 - Experience designing and running tabletop exercises, gamedays, or comparable readiness programs and translating findings into improvements..

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to represent technical tradeoffs to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

 - Experience mentoring engineers or otherwise raising the technical and investigative capabilities of a team.



How you'll work:

 - You look for opportunities to build systems that scale the team's capabilities rather than relying on repeated manual effort, and you're interested in thoughtfully applying AI and automation where they can improve security outcomes.

 - An experienced incident commander who brings structure to complex incidents, makes sound decisions with incomplete information, and helps teams move forward during high-pressure situations.

 - You're comfortable taking ownership of a capability from strategy through execution, including defining priorities, sequencing work, navigating dependencies, and delivering against a longer-term roadmap.

 - You can operate as a technical partner to leaders and cross-functional teams, independently representing technical priorities, risks, and tradeoffs.

 - You value continuous improvement and contribute to an environment where teams can examine incidents, decisions, and failures openly and turn what they learn into stronger systems and practices.



What you can expect:

 - Serve as incident manager and technical escalation point for complex, high-severity events, bringing structure, sound judgement, and clear decision-making under pressure.

 - Design and build AI-assisted and automated systems that improve how quickly and consistently the team can triage, investigate, and contain incidents.

 - Establish appropriate safety controls, approval gates, auditability, and rollback mechanisms for automated and AI-assisted actions, ensuring high-impact decisions remain appropriately human-controlled.

 - Own the team's readiness programs, including tabletop exercises and incident gamedays, from scenario design and execution through debriefing and translating finishes into concrete (or measurable) improvements

 - Advance the team’s threat hunting and insider risk capabilities by identifying opportunities, defining priorities, and delivering roadmap work that improves investigative depth and coverage

 - Plan, sequence, and deliver multi-quarter initiatives that mature the team's capabilities, bringing project management discipline to work that doesn't fit neatly into a sprint.

 - Mentor and provide technical leadership to other engineers, strengthening engineering rigor and investigative judgement across the team.

 - Partner with Security Operations, Product Security, and Engineering teams to close gaps surfaced through investigations, hunting, and simulations.

 - Foster psychological safety and blameless learning across incident retrospectives, gamedays, and tabletop debriefs.

 - Extend strong incident response practices beyond the immediate team by building reusable systems, tooling, and operating patterns that strengthen response capabilities across areas such as PSIRT, Privacy, and Engineering.



USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $192,000 USD and $278,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $167,000 CAD and $242,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits

Community

🌎 Remote-first work environment

 Design, implement, and test software written mainly in Go for our Linux-based appliances

 Practical experience with Kubernetes, containers, or orchestration platforms

 Clear communicator who enjoys cross-functional collaboration across software, firmware, cloud, and security teams  
 Fluent in French and English, both verbal and written (this role requires interaction with our international collaborators and customers)

 Hands-on work with K3s, Kubernetes internals, containerd, CNI, CSI, RBAC, network policies, or node lifecycle management  
 Practical experience in device fleet management (provisioning, enrollment, reconciliation of desired vs. reported state, secure remote access)  
 Background in security engineering for distributed systems (device identity, certificates, authorization, attestation, threat modeling, auditability)  
 Production experience operating cloud platforms at scale, ideally in multi-region architectures

 Familiarity with modern threat prevention technologies (sandboxing, CFI, ASLR, DEP, etc.).

Êtes-vous prêt(e) à faire progresser votre carrière tout en contribuant à un changement positif dans les marchés émergents? 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) associé(e) junior pour se joindre à notre équipe Infrastructures durables !
 Joignez-vous à FinDev Canada , l’institution de financement du développement du Canada! Nous travaillons avec et par l’intermédiaire du secteur privé pour faire progresser les actions en faveur du climat et de la nature, l’égalité des genres et le développement des marchés dans les économies en développement. Rejoindre FinDev Canada, c’est intégrer une organisation en pleine croissance, animée par une mission, au sein de laquelle votre expertise contribue directement à un impact significatif et mesurable à travers le monde..
 Type d’emploi : Contrat de 12 mois
 Lieu de travail : Le siège social de FinDev Canada est situé au centre-ville de Montréal. Pour la personne retenue, Ottawa ou Toronto pourront également être considérés. Le poste offre une formule de travail hybride, avec une présence minimale actuelle de trois jours par semaine au bureau (sous réserve de changements).
 Détails de la rémunération 
 Les salaires des étudiants, des nouveaux diplômés et des titulaires d’une maîtrise varient entre 42 900 $ et 56 550 $ par année , selon l’année d’études.
 Échelle salariale selon l’année d’études : 
 1re année : 42 900 $ (22,00 $/heure)
 2e année : 44 850 $ (23,00 $/heure)
 3e année : 46 800 $ (24,00 $/heure)
 4e année et plus : 48 750 $ (25,00 $/heure)
 Nouveau diplômé (baccalauréat) : 54 600 $ (28,00 $/heure)
 Maîtrise/doctorat : 56 550 $ (29,00 $/heure)
 Pourquoi vous aimerez travailler ici 
 Un travail porteur de sens 
 Nous sommes guidés par notre mandat visant à favoriser une croissance durable et inclusive dans les marchés émergents et les économies en développement. Chaque rôle contribue à créer un impact positif et durable pour nos clients, les marchés que nous servons et les communautés du monde entier.
 Des collègues inspirants 
 Joignez-vous à une équipe diversifiée et talentueuse provenant de partout dans le monde, qui met à profit une vaste expérience, de solides connaissances et une véritable passion dans tout ce qu’elle entreprend. Nous croyons que les meilleurs résultats reposent sur de solides partenariats, la collaboration, le partage des perspectives et la confiance mutuelle.
 Nos valeurs fondamentales 
 Notre culture repose sur la collaboration, l’agilité, l’impact et le respect . Nous travaillons en équipe, accueillons le changement et l’innovation, et demeurons centrés sur la création d’un impact durable et significatif, tout en traitant chacun avec intégrité, empathie et respect.
 Avantages et récompenses globales 
 Notre offre de rémunération globale va bien au-delà du salaire. Nous proposons un ensemble complet d’avantages conçu pour répondre aux besoins variés et aux différentes étapes de vie de nos employés.
 Aperçu de l’équipe 
 L’équipe Infrastructures durables de FinDev Canada fait partie du groupe Investissements. Elle est responsable de l’origination, de la structuration, de la documentation, de l’obtention des approbations de crédit et de la conclusion de solutions de financement sur mesure destinées à soutenir des entreprises du secteur privé dans les marchés émergents et les économies en développement.
 L’équipe se concentre sur les investissements dans des secteurs tels que les énergies renouvelables, le transport, l’eau et l’assainissement, ainsi que les infrastructures numériques. Ces investissements soutiennent les priorités de développement de FinDev Canada en favorisant l’atténuation des changements climatiques, la création d’emplois et l’autonomisation économique des femmes.
 Ce poste représente une excellente occasion pour un diplômé récent ou un professionnel en début de carrière d’acquérir une expérience fondamentale en investissement dans les infrastructures et en financement du développement, tout en travaillant aux côtés de professionnels chevronnés sur des transactions ayant un impact concret.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Soutenir les responsables d’investissement dans l’évaluation et l’exécution des transactions d’investissement.
 Réaliser des analyses financières, de crédit et de marché afin d’appuyer la prise de décision en matière d’investissement.
 Participer à l’analyse préliminaire et à l’évaluation de nouvelles occasions d’investissement.
 Appuyer les activités de diligence raisonnable, notamment en recueillant et en analysant l’information provenant des clients et de sources externes.
 Contribuer à l’élaboration et à la mise à jour de modèles financiers.
 Préparer des notes d’investissement internes, des présentations et d’autres documents liés aux transactions.
 Effectuer des recherches sectorielles, de marché et par pays afin de soutenir le développement des affaires et l’exécution des transactions.
 Collaborer avec les spécialistes internes afin d’intégrer les considérations environnementales, sociales, de gouvernance (ESG) et d’impact sur le développement dans les évaluations d’investissement.
 Fournir un soutien général tout au long du cycle de vie des investissements avant leur clôture.
 Ce que nous recherchons 
 Être actuellement aux études ou avoir obtenu, au cours de la dernière année, un diplôme de premier cycle ou de deuxième cycle dans un domaine pertinent, notamment la finance, l’économie, l’administration des affaires, le commerce ou une discipline connexe.
 Posséder de 0 à 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente, y compris des stages, des programmes coopératifs ou une expérience comme analyste en finance, infrastructures, consultation, services bancaires ou domaines connexes.
 Démontrer de solides compétences analytiques, quantitatives et de résolution de problèmes.
 Être capable de synthétiser l’information et de présenter les résultats de façon claire et efficace.
 Faire preuve d’excellentes aptitudes organisationnelles et d’un grand souci du détail.
 Démontrer un intérêt marqué pour le développement durable, les infrastructures, l’investissement d’impact ou le financement du développement.
 Posséder d’excellentes aptitudes en communication écrite et orale.
 Être bilingue dans les deux langues officielles (français et anglais).
 Ce qui vous permettra de vous démarquer 
 Expérience en modélisation financière, analyse d’investissement, crédit, consultation ou financement de projets.
 Connaissance des secteurs des infrastructures, notamment l’énergie, le transport, l’eau, l’assainissement ou les infrastructures numériques.
 Connaissance des cadres ESG, de durabilité, de financement climatique ou de mesure d’impact sur le développement.
 Progression vers une désignation professionnelle telle que le CFA ou le CPA.
 Expérience dans un contexte international, dans les marchés émergents ou dans un environnement axé sur le développement.
 Prêt(e) à faire une différence? 
 Pour en savoir davantage sur nous : https://www.findevcanada.ca 
 Admissibilité 
 FinDev Canada s’engage à appliquer des pratiques d’emploi équitables. La préférence sera accordée aux candidats qui sont légalement autorisés à travailler au Canada au moment de leur candidature (citoyens canadiens ou résidents permanents).
 Les candidats doivent satisfaire aux exigences de sécurité du gouvernement applicables. Le poste est ouvert aux personnes qui répondent à toutes les exigences essentielles énoncées ci-dessus et dont la candidature est reçue avant la date limite.
 Votre candidature doit démontrer clairement comment vous répondez à toutes les exigences. Nous remercions toutes les personnes qui manifestent leur intérêt pour une carrière à FinDev Canada. Toutefois, seules les personnes retenues pour une entrevue seront contactées.
 Veuillez noter que les candidats qualifiés pourraient également être pris en considération pour des postes similaires de même niveau au sein de FinDev Canada.
 L’engagement de FinDev Canada envers l’équité en matière d’emploi 
 FinDev Canada s’engage à promouvoir l’équité en matière d’emploi et à bâtir un effectif diversifié. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement sécuritaire et inclusif qui respecte les personnes de toutes les cultures, origines et capacités.
 Chez FinDev Canada, nous favorisons une culture d’inclusion et d’appartenance où chacun a les mêmes possibilités de grandir, de se perfectionner, de réussir et d’être pleinement lui-même.
 Nous encourageons activement les candidatures des femmes, des peuples autochtones, des minorités visibles, des personnes en situation de handicap et des membres de la communauté 2ELGBTQI+.
 FinDev Canada reconnaît que divulguer un besoin d’adaptation peut être une démarche personnelle. Soyez assuré que nous nous engageons à préserver la confidentialité et à offrir des mesures d’adaptation adaptées à vos besoins.
 Notre objectif est de vous offrir une expérience positive et inclusive tout au long du processus de recrutement. N’hésitez pas à communiquer avec nous à accessible@findevcanada.ca pour toute demande d’adaptation. Nous sommes là pour vous accompagner à chaque étape.
 Avis de confidentialité 
 En soumettant votre candidature, vous reconnaissez avoir lu et compris l’Avis de confidentialité de FinDev Canada à l’intention des candidats, qui décrit la façon dont nous recueillons, utilisons, conservons et protégeons les renseignements personnels durant le processus de recrutement, ainsi que vos droits d’accès et de rectification.

 Manage the contractual commitments of contractors, including cost, quality, and schedule and coordinate their field activities.
 Plan and manage the project’s temporary facilities.

 Administer, train, and motivate all personnel in construction operations

 The Quick Version 
 Have you ever seen a company create their own National Holiday as part of its marketing efforts? 
 We did!
 Speaking of silly stuff, we even wrote and produced our own comedic commercial about the real pains that our customers have, and it helped make one of our tools the fastest growing AI tool in the industry! 
 Ultimately we want our marketing to be funny, human, and memorable, because honestly a lot of the stuff out there in the government industry (which is where we compete) is boring. 
 Now we're looking for someone exceptionally creative to lead our marketing department — a person with the freedom to take big creative swings and the resources to execute their own.
 Our brands — Town Web, HeyGov, and ClerkMinutes — form a suite of tools built specifically for municipal clerks, and each one is crafted to be exceptional at its job. If you're a highly effective, exceptional marketing professional, we'd love for you to apply. Below are more details about who we are and what we're trying to achieve.
 Here's a video to tell you more about this role !
 The details 
 Who we are
 We're a small, bootstrapped company approaching $3M in ARR, competing against large, private-equity-owned firms with far deeper pockets. That's why our marketing has to be exceptional on two fronts at once: creative work that is unique and memorable, and follow-through to match it — multi-channel campaigns, disciplined measurement, and sophisticated execution that turns attention into pipeline.
 Our customers are municipal clerks at cities, counties, and municipalities of all sizes. They are busy, under-resourced, deeply practical, and they talk to each other (which as you can guess is why we are emphasising the need to have exceptional marketing!)
 We build focused products for the clerk specifically, designed to work together as a suite. ClerkMinutes became one of the most widely adopted tools in its category largely on the strength of marketing that looked like nothing else in this space, and your job is to push that further across the whole portfolio. We run on EOS, and the marketing department's cadence — L10s, quarterly Rocks, scorecards — will be yours to run.
 What you'll own
 Strategy and positioning across the portfolio, and the department's EOS operating cadence
 Demand and revenue — building a qualified pipeline for Sales through targeted campaigns and similar initiatives. This is how success is measured. 
 Full-channel execution — conferences, webinars, direct mail, PR, and outbound alongside digital and paid. Clerks trust people who show up in person, so you will too.
 Lifecycle marketing — from first touch through trial to customer, along with the tech, tracking, and attribution behind it
 The quality bar — you're the final day-to-day reviewer on copy, design, campaigns, and launches
 Go-to-market with Product and Sales — new product launches and targeted campaigns that get us early beta testers, help build awareness for product pilots, and than formal product releases.

 Isn’t it clear we’re looking for somebody extremely creative and ambitious!? 😛Are you “THE ONE?”

Think of a special-forces team leader: they plan the mission, and when it's time to move, they're also the first one through the door. That's the posture this role needs — you set the strategy, and then you're in the weeds executing it right alongside the team.
 And there is a team. You'll work directly with our copywriters, internal product managers, the sales team, and the people who handle data connection and attribution through Salesforce and our other marketing tools. You'll have a team around you, but want to be clear: we’re not looking for a “manager of managers”.
 AI tools like Claude or Codex are part of your daily workflow, and you rely on them to get competent quickly in unfamiliar territory, whether that's GEO, GA4, or something we haven't thought of yet. You also know how to work with a highly creative founder: turning a lot of ideas into focused priorities, pushing back when something won't work, and making sure the good ones actually ship.
 This role suits someone who's comfortable working without a finished playbook, and who would rather be in the work than above it.
 What we need to see
 Exceptional Enthusiasm
 Extremely Creative Energy
 You've led a marketing function and been accountable for its results
 You've made a traditional or crowded category stand out with ideas of your own
 AI is central to how you work, and you're comfortable enough with code to build or fix small things yourself
 Real paid acquisition experience across Meta, Google, LinkedIn, and Bing, and you can run SEO and GEO by directing AI tools well
 Hands-on experience with direct mail, paid ads, conferences, PR, or other high-attention channels, and you're happy traveling to meet clerks and work conferences alongside Sales
 B2B SaaS background, and you've managed employees, contractors, and agencies
 Nice to have: GovTech or public-sector experience, marketing more than one product at a time, and building measurement where little existed. EOS familiarity helps too!

 Complete the Workable Form, and make sure to include your resume.
 There will questions to answer. Please make sure you answer them- we read these!

Nous recherchons un(e) Spécialiste de la paie expérimenté(e) et minutieux(se) pour gérer et soutenir les activités de paie de nos opérations au Canada et aux États-Unis. Il s'agit d'un rôle pratique responsable de veiller à ce que la paie soit traitée avec exactitude, dans les délais, et conformément aux exigences applicables en matière de paie, de fiscalité et de rapports.
  Le/la Spécialiste de la paie travaillera principalement avec les Ressources humaines pour examiner et résoudre les problèmes liés à la paie, en veillant à ce que les préoccupations des employés soient traitées de façon précise, cohérente et conforme aux politiques de l'entreprise et à la législation applicable. Ce rôle collaborera également avec les Finances, les superviseurs, les gestionnaires, les fournisseurs de services de paie et d'autres partenaires selon les besoins.
  Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) possède une solide expérience en paie canadienne, y compris une expérience avec la paie Desjardins, ainsi qu'une connaissance pratique de la paie américaine. Une expérience à l'appui de la mise en œuvre ou de la transition d'un système de paie ou de SIRH constituerait un atout important.
 Responsabilités 
 Gérer et traiter les cycles de paie réguliers pour les employés au Canada et aux États-Unis, en veillant à l'exactitude et à l'exécution dans les délais.
 Examiner, valider et traiter les changements liés à la paie, y compris les nouvelles embauches, les cessations d'emploi, les changements de rémunération, les primes, les déductions, les avantages sociaux et autres mises à jour concernant les employés.
 Importer et rapprocher les données de feuilles de temps et de suivi du temps, en collaborant avec les RH et les superviseurs pour résoudre les écarts avant le traitement de la paie.
 Collaborer principalement avec les Ressources humaines pour enquêter sur les préoccupations, écarts et problèmes liés à la rémunération des employés, et les résoudre.
 Appuyer les RH dans la réponse aux questions des employés concernant la paie et veiller à ce que les problèmes soient traités de façon cohérente, professionnelle et confidentielle.
 Traiter les vacances, les congés de maladie, les congés payés et autres absences liées à la paie conformément aux politiques de l'entreprise et à la législation applicable.
 Collaborer avec les RH pour traiter les exigences de paie liées aux congés de maternité ou parentaux, congés de maladie, invalidité, congés sans solde et retours de congé des employés.
 Traiter les paies finales, les indemnités de vacances et autres exigences de paie liées aux cessations d'emploi.
 Appuyer la préparation et l'administration des Relevés d'emploi (RE) et d'autres documents de paie requis au Canada.
 Veiller à ce que les impôts sur la paie, les déductions statutaires et les cotisations de l'employeur soient calculés et versés avec exactitude.
 Préparer les déclarations fiscales liées à la paie, les rapprochements et les rapports gouvernementaux requis.
 Coordonner et appuyer les activités de paie de fin d'année, y compris les T4, les RL-1, les W-2 et autres rapports de fin d'année applicables.
 Résoudre les écarts liés à la paie et à la fiscalité, selon les besoins.
 Préparer les rapports de paie, les rapprochements et la documentation d'appui pour les Finances, les Ressources humaines et d'autres parties prenantes internes.
 Fournir la documentation et le soutien nécessaires à la paie pour les audits internes et externes.
 Maintenir des contrôles de paie appropriés et veiller à ce que les renseignements de paie des employés soient traités avec exactitude et confidentialité.
 Aider aux rapprochements de comptes et aux rapports liés à la paie, selon les besoins des Finances.
 Aider à répondre aux exigences liées à la paie lors de la transition ou de la mise en œuvre de nouveaux systèmes de RH, de paie et de suivi du temps par l'organisation.
 Coordonner avec les fournisseurs de services de paie externes, les organismes gouvernementaux, les fournisseurs d'avantages sociaux et d'autres partenaires, selon les besoins.
 Exigences
 3 ans ou plus d'expérience pratique de la paie au Québec, idéalement en soutenant à la fois la paie canadienne et américaine.
 À l'aise pour parler et écrire en français et en anglais.
 Solide connaissance des pratiques de paie du Québec, de la fiscalité, des déductions statutaires, du traitement de fin d'année et de la conformité en matière de paie.
 Expérience du traitement de la paie avec Desjardins / Employeur D.
 Familiarité avec les pratiques de paie américaines, les impôts sur la paie, les déductions et les exigences de fin d'année.
 Expérience avec les systèmes de suivi du temps ainsi que l'importation et le rapprochement des feuilles de temps.
 Expérience du traitement des vacances, des congés, des cessations d'emploi et d'autres changements liés au cycle de vie des employés, du point de vue de la paie.
 Une expérience antérieure à l'appui de la mise en œuvre, de la conversion ou de la transition d'un système de paie ou de SIRH est considérée comme un atout important.
 Expérience à l'appui des audits de paie et de la préparation de rapprochements et de rapports de paie.
 Solides compétences en Excel et aisance avec les données de paie.

 We are looking for an experienced, detail-oriented Payroll Specialist to manage and support payroll activities across our Canadian and U.S. operations. This is a hands-on role responsible for ensuring payroll is processed accurately, on time, and in compliance with applicable payroll, tax, and reporting requirements.
 The Payroll Specialist will work primarily with Human Resources to review and resolve payroll-related issues, ensuring employee concerns are addressed accurately, consistently, and in accordance with company policies and applicable legislation. This role will also work with Finance, supervisors, managers, payroll providers, and other partners as required.
 The ideal candidate has strong Canadian payroll experience, including experience with Desjardins payroll, as well as working knowledge of U.S. payroll. Experience supporting a payroll or HRIS system implementation or transition would be a strong asset.
 Responsibilities: 
 Manage and process regular payroll cycles for employees in Canada and the United States, ensuring accuracy and timely completion.
 Review, validate, and process payroll changes, including new hires, terminations, compensation changes, bonuses, deductions, benefits, and other employee updates.
 Import and reconcile timecard and timekeeping data, working with HR and supervisors to resolve discrepancies before payroll is processed.
 Partner primarily with Human Resources to investigate and resolve employee payroll concerns, discrepancies, and pay-related issues.
 Support HR in responding to employee payroll questions and ensure issues are handled consistently, professionally, and confidentially.
 Process vacation, sick time, paid time off, and other payroll-related absences in accordance with company policies and applicable legislation.
 Partner with HR to process payroll requirements related to maternity or parental leaves, medical leaves, disability, unpaid leaves, and employee returns from leave.
 Process final pays, vacation payouts, and other termination-related payroll requirements.
 Support the preparation and administration of Records of Employment (ROEs) and other required payroll documentation in Canada.
 Ensure payroll taxes, statutory deductions, and employer contributions are calculated and remitted accurately.
 Prepare payroll tax filings, reconciliations, and required government reporting.
 Coordinate and support year-end payroll activities, including T4s, RL-1s, W-2s, and other applicable year-end reporting.
 Resolve payroll and tax discrepancies as required.
 Prepare payroll reports, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for Finance, Human Resources, and other internal stakeholders.
 Provide payroll documentation and support for internal and external audits.
 Maintain appropriate payroll controls and ensure employee payroll information is handled accurately and confidentially.
 Assist with payroll-related account reconciliations and reporting as required by Finance.
 Assist with payroll-related requirements as the organization transitions or implements new HR, payroll, and timekeeping systems.
 Coordinate with external payroll providers, government agencies, benefits providers, and other partners as required.
 Requirements 
 3+ years of hands-on Quebec payroll experience, ideally supporting both Canadian and U.S. payroll.
 Comfortable speaking and writing in both French and English.
 Strong knowledge of Quebec payroll practices, taxation, statutory deductions, year-end processing, and payroll compliance.
 Experience processing payroll using Desjardins / Employer D.
 Familiarity with U.S. payroll practices, payroll taxes, deductions, and year-end requirements.
 Experience with timekeeping systems and timecard imports and reconciliation.
 Experience processing vacation, leaves of absence, terminations, and other employee lifecycle changes from a payroll perspective.
 Previous experience supporting a payroll or HRIS implementation, conversion, or system transition is considered a strong asset.
 Experience supporting payroll audits and preparing payroll reconciliations and reports.
 Strong Excel skills and comfort working with payroll data. 
 Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to meet strict payroll deadlines.

 different protection strategies for IBRs, such as anti-islanding protection.

We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.




OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.



Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.




AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring Float's first Staff Security Engineer, to own the technical direction of our security platform: application, infrastructure and identity security. Our security team is small and builds more than it buys. We write our own detections, run our own agent platform, and fix things at the root. Float's engineers build quickly and we don't run big security gates, so your job is to make the secure path the easy one. You'll take a complex area of security, own it from end to end, and design the fixes alongside engineering, then drive them through to adoption across product teams. You'll look ahead too, setting up the foundations for new products, and for how we run AI tools safely, well before teams start building. You'll work as a peer to our staff and principal engineers, and explain big architectural changes and the risk behind them in a way that moves everyone toward the outcome.




WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own the technical strategy for security platform work: set standards, write down decisions, and explain risk to leadership in business terms.

 - Own a major area of security end to end, from the risks and the plan through to shipped improvements.

 - Build security primitives into our core backend (Python and Django), such as default-closed authorization and tenancy scoping, then lead adoption across every product team.

 - Shape our customer identity platform: passwords, passkeys, SSO/SAML and machine-to-machine authentication.

 - Threat model and review the architecture and code of new products and large changes, and help redesign things so they are better, not only point out what's wrong.

 - Secure how we use AI: our internal agent platform, MCP gateways, and the data that flows through them.

 - Look ahead and put security foundations in place about six months before teams start building in a new area.

 - Lead multi-quarter efforts across several engineers as the security voice in the room, with minimal drag on engineering delivery, and mentor engineers on and off the security team.

 - Present significant architectural and engineering changes, with the risks, to engineers and leaders so they understand and act.

 - Harden our CI/CD and software supply chain, and turn controls into code (infrastructure as code, policy as code) instead of manual work.

 - Help secure the platform as we move to Kubernetes: workload isolation, network policy, IAM and secrets.

 - Build in-house tools and capabilities where it makes more sense than buying them as Float grows.

 - Give timely, practical advice early in the process so teams spend less time waiting on security.

 - Identify blind spots across the company and help set priorities for where security should invest.

 - Use AI tools to move faster on threat modelling, reviews, investigation and building.




ABOUT YOU

Here's what sets you up for success at Float:

 - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.

 - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.

 - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.

 - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.

 - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 8+ years of experience as a software engineer or security engineer, at a company large enough that you built systems and tools yourself.

 - Depth in at least one of application security, identity, or cloud and infrastructure security, and credibility across the rest.

 - You ship production code to fix what you find, in Python and Django or a similar web stack.

 - Hands-on experience designing and building security controls, tooling or systems, and the engineering depth to be a peer to staff-level engineers.

 - You've led a multi-quarter, cross-team technical change through influence, not authority.

 - A real interest in security, shown by what you've built, learned or owned.

 - Experience owning a complex technical problem and shipping it from start to finish.

 - Clear, direct writing and communication with engineers and leaders, able to explain architecture and risk in business terms in a way that leads to action.

 - Practical examples of using AI in your engineering or security work.

 - Nice to haves:
   
   - Fintech, payments or PCI DSS experience.
   
   - Building or running an identity platform at scale.
   
   - Detection engineering or incident response.
   
   - Experience securing LLM or agent systems.
   
   - Experience with container and Kubernetes infrastructure security.
   
   - Experience bringing a bought tool in-house.




THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF

 - You prefer to report findings and leave the fixes to others, or you don't ship production code.

 - You'd rather ship a fix once than drive it through adoption across many teams.

 - You like to act as a gatekeeper, with a firm "must" and a firm "no", more than as a partner to engineering.

 - Your experience is mainly configuring and running purchased security products or managing compliance.

 - You'd rather be embedded in implementation than set direction and bring others along.

 - You're resistant to AI-enabled ways of working.




OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

We hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Titles matter less than impact, and every hire is expected to raise the bar for Float as a whole.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

 - Be part of an award winning company: we're one of Canada’s Top Growing Companies 2026 according to Report on Business, and Deloitte’s Technology Fast50 2026

 - Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role

 - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team

 - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits

 - Hybrid work model: we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration

 - Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday

 - Bring your pup to our dog-friendly office

 - Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters




IN SHORT

At Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special—and having a lot of fun along the way. If you’re excited to build, grow, and win together, we’d love to meet you.



Protect yourself from recruiting scams. Float only contacts candidates from @floatfinancial.com http://floatfinancial.com addresses and schedules interviews through Ashby or Float calendar invites. We will never ask you to install software, pay a fee, buy equipment or share bank or card details. If something looks off, don't engage.



We’re committed to building a workplace that’s welcoming and accessible for everyone. If you need any accommodations during the hiring process or once you join Float, just let us know! You can reach out to Vic https://www.linkedin.com/in/victoria-boult-b21b2053/ (victoria@floatfinancial.com), and we’ll work with you to make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Détails du poste

 Type de poste : Temps plein, permanent.
 Début visé : janvier 2027.
 À propos d'elia 
 elia est la plateforme tout-en-un d'opérations des espaces de travail des grandes organisations. Réservation de bureaux et de salles, gestion des visiteurs, capteurs d'occupation, casiers intelligents, affichage numérique, gestion d'actifs : on réunit tout dans une seule plateforme. Des grandes organisations nous font confiance, au Canada, aux États-Unis et ailleurs dans le monde. Nous sommes aujourd'hui une équipe d'une quarantaine de personnes en forte croissance, et nous prévoyons passer à environ 120 personnes au cours des 3 prochaines années. Chaque personne a un impact direct sur le produit et sur la façon dont on bâtit l'entreprise, et l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de travailler.
 Le rôle 
 Demandez à n'importe qui qui gère les bureaux d'une grande organisation à quoi ressemble sa semaine : salles de réunion réservées en double, bureaux vides le vendredi et pris d'assaut le mercredi, visiteurs qui attendent à l'accueil parce que personne ne les attendait, cinq outils différents qui ne se parlent pas.
 elia règle ça avec une seule plateforme pour les équipes qui gèrent le milieu de travail : gestion des installations, TI et RH. Certaines des plus grandes organisations privées et publiques du Québec roulent déjà leur milieu de travail sur elia, et nous voulons rejoindre les prochaines.
 Comme SDR, vous ouvrez la porte. Vous appelez des gens dans de grandes organisations du Québec, vous amorcez de vraies conversations sur la façon dont leur milieu de travail fonctionne, et vous obtenez les appels découverte que nos Account Executives transforment en contrats. C'est un poste d'appels à froid en grand volume, principalement en français.
 Responsabilités 
 Faire un grand volume d'appels à froid chaque jour auprès d'une liste définie de grandes organisations du Québec (500 employés et plus), principalement en français.
 Utiliser le téléphone comme canal principal, appuyé par le courriel et LinkedIn.
 Faire de la recherche sur chaque compte avant de le contacter, pour que chaque appel ait une vraie raison d'être.
 Obtenir des appels découverte avec les bonnes personnes en gestion des installations, milieu de travail, immobilier, TI et RH.
 Rédiger une note de transfert claire pour chaque appel : qui y participe, quel problème la personne a probablement, et pourquoi maintenant.
 S'assurer que les prospects se présentent, et programmer l'appel au besoin.
 Travailler de près avec nos Account Executives du Québec pour choisir les comptes à cibler chaque mois.
 Garder HubSpot à jour (« Si ce n'est pas dans le CRM, ça n'est pas arrivé »).
 Profil recherché 
 Excellent français, parlé et écrit, naturel au téléphone. Vous passerez vos journées en appels avec des décideurs québécois, et l'aisance en français fait une différence visible dans les résultats.
 L'anglais est un atout important : il nous permettrait de vous faire évoluer vers d'autres marchés.
 Idéalement, de l'expérience en appels à froid ou en prospection : rôle de SDR, télémarketing, recrutement, ventes internes (peu importe l'industrie, vous n'avez pas besoin de connaître la nôtre).
 Les finissant-es et jeunes diplômé-es motivé-es par une carrière en vente sont les bienvenu-es (l'expérience vous donne un avantage, la motivation vous ouvre la porte).
 À l'aise au téléphone toute la journée : vous appelez les gens, vous ne vous cachez pas derrière le courriel.
 Résilience : la plupart des appels restent sans réponse, et vous continuez quand même.
 Curiosité pour le fonctionnement des entreprises, et discipline de faire vos recherches d'abord.
 À l'aise avec les technologies 
 Vous devez être à l'aise avec les technologies et utiliser déjà des outils d'IA dans votre travail au quotidien.
 On cherche quelqu'un de technophile, qui comprend bien les plateformes et qui est curieux de tester différents outils.

About us:  
 At Red Rabbit Robotics, our mission is to tackle the global labor shortage and create a future of abundance. We aim to deploy one million humanoid robots in the next 10 years. Our robots are designed to tackle manual labor across manufacturing, warehouse, logistics and more. Our “teleoperation first” strategy immediately delivers value by providing humanoid labor as a service through remote operators, while simultaneously building a powerful data flywheel that fuels the foundation models for robotics and leads to full autonomy for physical world AI.
 Founded just a few months ago, we have already built two generations of humanoid robot prototypes, secured venture backing, and attracted major customers eager to try out our solution. With real time human oversight and a powerful data flywheel, we are building embodied AI systems that can work in the real world in the same way as we do. Check out our prototype demo videos at www.redrabbitrobotics.ai .
 What we believe: 
 We are all about our customers. We talk to real folks in the industry to find out what they actually need, then we build products that solve those problems. Simple as that.
 We are agnostic to different technical approaches. There is no single “silver bullet” for real world robotics. We stay open-minded, keep learning, and try whatever works best.
 We keep it practical. For example, our robots have wheels, not legs (no backflips in the near future). We don’t waste time over-engineering fancy features that don’t make a real difference for our customers’ success.
 The role: 
 We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to own the design and implementation of our humanoid robot’s control systems. A major responsibility in this role is helping us evaluate and select the right technology stack. You’ll be deeply involved in real-time control loops, sensor fusion, actuator integration, and higher-level motion planning algorithms. This role is in person for our Vancouver, Canada office.
 What you will do: 
 Design, implement, and optimize real-time control architectures (manipulation, navigation, teleoperation).
 Investigate and compare frameworks and algorithms to guide our core software platform decisions.
 Integrate sensors (LiDAR, vision, IMU, force/torque) and actuators (BLDC servo motors).
 Develop algorithms for motion planning, kinematics, and advanced control strategies.
 Collaborate closely with hardware and operations teams to ensure cohesive system integration.
 Create testing procedures for both simulation and real hardware to validate performance and reliability.
 What you will bring: 
 Proficiency in C++ or Rust (experience with ROS/ROS2 is a big plus).
 Strong foundation in control theory, kinematics, and dynamics of robotic systems.
 Proven track record of shipping code code for commercial or open-source robotics projects that have high impacts. 
 Experience with real-time embedded systems and safety-critical software.
 Excellent problem-solving skills and a willingness to adapt and learn.
 Hands on experience building and debugging electrical and mechanical systems.
 Knowledge of machine learning for robotics and advanced motion planning.
 Background using simulation tools like Gazebo, Mujuco or Nvidia Isaac Sim.
 Being able to speak Chinese and communicating with our vendors directly is a bonus.
 This role requires shifting working schedules and travelling to the US from time to time.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

Adoption of AI is moving rapidly from pilots to production. Enterprises are investing in generative-AI programs, creating a once-in-a-decade market inflection point. At Cohere, we’re committed to transforming the enterprise landscape through strategic partnerships and innovative AI solutions. As a Partner Development Manager for the Enterprise Market, you’ll be at the heart of our mission to empower businesses across the region with cutting-edge AI technologies.

This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a dynamic, cross-cultural environment and is passionate about driving growth through collaboration. You’ll work closely with leading enterprises, system integrators, and technology partners to co-create value, expand market reach, and deliver impactful AI solutions tailored to the unique needs of businesses.

Your work will directly contribute to our success. You’ll have the opportunity to shape partnerships that drive digital transformation, foster innovation, and position Cohere as a leader in the AI ecosystem.

Partner Strategy & Execution

 - Owns AWS-sourced and AWS-influenced Cohere pipeline — activating AWS field sales and technical teams to select and deploy Cohere

Pipeline Generation & Co-Selling

Partner Advocacy & Feedback

Thought Leadership & Evangelism

Why You’ll Love This Role

This is a high-impact role where you’ll shape the future of AI partnerships.  We are seeking a Senior Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help guide lighting execution across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on senior role with leadership responsibilities. In addition to producing lighting work, you will review the work of other artists, provide clear direction and feedback, help organize lighting tasks, and ensure that scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate closely with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios. You will help translate creative direction into practical lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, narrative, and performance.
 This role may oversee the day-to-day work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting. It does not necessarily include formal people-management responsibilities, but it requires accountability for team output, effective mentorship, and the ability to raise concerns when work is at risk of missing quality, schedule, or technical expectations.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, gameplay requirements, lighting pipeline, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, Engineering, clients, and partner teams.
 Create polished lighting work that demonstrates the expected visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for an assigned level, environment, sequence, or group of scenes.
 Review work from other artists and provide timely, actionable feedback that improves quality and consistency.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and work with project leadership to resolve them.
 Help the team deliver lighting work that meets milestone expectations for quality, performance, and completeness.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Artistic Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.
 Maintain consistency across connected environments, gameplay spaces, cinematics, times of day, weather conditions, and lighting scenarios.
 Bring assigned scenes to final quality while meeting technical requirements and production deadlines.
 Leadership and Quality Oversight
 Oversee lighting work for an assigned area of the project, such as a level, world region, sequence, feature, or milestone.
 Review the work of lighting artists and other contributors whose work affects the final lighting result.
 Provide clear, constructive, and actionable feedback through live reviews, written notes, paintovers, reference boards, documentation, and in-engine examples.
 Ensure lighting work follows the visual direction, technical standards, and quality expectations established by Art Direction and the client.
 Help artists understand priorities, expected outcomes, acceptance criteria, and the level of polish required for each milestone.
 Track the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that require additional support, revision, or escalation.
 Verify that feedback has been addressed and that completed work meets the established quality bar before submission.
 Mentor junior and mid-level artists in lighting fundamentals, technical execution, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.
 Lead by example through strong artistic execution, professional communication, reliable follow-through, and practical problem-solving.
 Help resolve differing artistic opinions by referring decisions back to approved visual targets, gameplay needs, technical constraints, and project priorities.
 Escalate unresolved quality, scope, staffing, scheduling, or technical risks to the appropriate project leads.
 Planning and Production Support
 Work with Art Direction and Production to break down lighting goals into clear tasks, priorities, estimates, and milestone deliverables.
 Help assess lighting scope, scene complexity, dependencies, and production risks.
 Support task assignment based on artist strengths, project priorities, and schedule needs.
 Provide progress updates and communicate when work is likely to miss visual, technical, or scheduling expectations.
 Participate in daily reviews, milestone evaluations, client reviews, and project-planning discussions.
 Help prepare lighting work for internal reviews, client presentations, milestone submissions, and final delivery.
 Balance hands-on production responsibilities with review, mentorship, troubleshooting, and team support.
 Adapt plans and priorities when creative direction, production scope, technical requirements, or client feedback changes.
 Technical and Pipeline Responsibilities
 Partner with Technical Art and Engineering to ensure lighting solutions are visually effective, technically stable, and appropriate for the target platform.
 Work within established budgets for frame rate, dynamic lights, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, global illumination, memory, and scalability.
 Diagnose and resolve issues involving exposure, shadow artifacts, light leaking, reflections, global illumination, volumetrics, bake quality, material response, and post-processing.
 Determine when to use dynamic, baked, stationary, or hybrid lighting approaches based on project requirements.
 Profile lighting work and make informed visual tradeoffs to meet performance requirements.
 Validate lighting across relevant gameplay cameras, display settings, hardware targets, times of day, weather states, and scalability levels.
 Help develop and maintain reusable lighting setups, templates, documentation, validation processes, and best practices.
 Identify workflow inefficiencies and recommend practical improvements to Art Direction, Technical Art, or Production.
 Follow project standards for scene organization, naming conventions, source control, documentation, and asset integration.
 Cross-Discipline Collaboration
 Collaborate with Environment Art to ensure geometry, materials, composition, and set dressing support the intended lighting.
 Partner with VFX to integrate fog, particles, weather, fire, emissive effects, and atmospheric elements.
 Work with Design to ensure lighting supports navigation, player guidance, combat readability, objectives, and interactive systems.
 Coordinate with Character Art and Animation to maintain readable and appealing character presentation in gameplay and cinematics.
 Partner with Cinematics teams on shot composition, continuity, exposure, character lighting, and narrative focus.
 Communicate artistic and technical tradeoffs clearly to both creative and non-creative stakeholders.
 Work effectively with distributed teams, partner studios, external vendors, and clients across different time zones.
 Requirements
 Professional experience creating lighting for games, real-time projects, or a closely related field.
 At least one shipped game or comparable professional real-time project.
 A portfolio or reel demonstrating high-quality real-time lighting.
 Strong understanding of lighting fundamentals, including value, color, contrast, composition, visual hierarchy, atmosphere, exposure, shadow, and material response.
 Experience lighting gameplay environments and interactive real-time scenes.

 Professional experience using Unreal Engine or another modern real-time engine.

 Maya, Blender, 3ds Max, or another 3D content-creation package
 Perforce or another production source-control system

Share in something more with a career at COBS Bread 
 Great Place to Work® Certified™ and one of Canada’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in 2026 
 Our Role 
 At COBS Bread, we believe in baking fresh, delicious bread every day for our community. Join our team as a Baker and play a key role in creating artisan bread that customers love. We offer a supportive and fun environment where you can grow your skills and be part of a passionate team.
 Your Role as Baker 
 As a Baker, you will help prepare and bake a wide variety of bread products by following established recipes and processes. You will work in a close-knit team to ensure that every bakery item meets COBS' quality and freshness standards.
 Responsibilities 
 Prepare, mix, and shape dough according to recipes and production schedules
 Operate ovens and other baking equipment safely and efficiently
 Maintain a clean and organized bakery environment
 Assist team members with daily baking tasks and provide excellent customer service as needed
 Follow health and safety and food safety guidelines strictly
 Qualifications and Requirements 
 Ability to work early morning shifts, typically starting between midnight and 4 am
 Comfortable working both independently and collaboratively in a small team
 Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
 Positive attitude with a willingness to learn and grow
 Physical ability to stand for extended periods and handle lifting up to 22 kg
 Previous baking experience is an asset but not required
 Food safe certification and basic first aid are assets
 Commitment to upholding COBS Bread quality and safety standards
 Perks & What You’ll Feel Good About 
 The satisfaction of baking from scratch, and pride in sharing that product with the community.
 A fun team work environment with flexible hours
 Our training program – Continue to develop your baking and leadership skills through our Bronze and Silver baker Development Qualification program.
 Career advancement opportunities – We have a stake in helping passionate team members grow and have more impact in the business and community.
 Complimentary products on us every shift
 And more, including benefits for all full time employees
 While we thank you for your interest, only those selected for interviews will be contacted.
 About COBS Bread 
 With over 130 locations, COBS Bread serves fresh and delightful baked goods to communities across Canada every day. Any unsold items are donated daily to various local charities and food banks. The company's success can be attributed to the quality of our product, the development of our people, and our warm and friendly customer service.
 COBS Bread is part of Bakers Delight – Established in 1980 operating as Bakers Delight in Australia and New Zealand, and since 2003 as COBS Bread in Canada and the USA. Together we have grown to more than 700 bakeries across Australia, New Zealand, Canada and the USA. The entire network employs over 15,000 people, serving more than 2.1 million customers each week.
 Accessibility 
 Accommodation is available upon request for applicants and employees with disabilities. If you are contacted for a job opportunity, please advise us of any accommodations needed to ensure you have access to a fair and equitable process. Any information received relating to accommodation will be addressed confidentially.

Suivez votre étoile!
 Si vous êtes passionné(e) par les enjeux environnementaux et souhaitez jouer un rôle concret dans la construction d’un avenir durable, rejoignez Norda Stelo. Faites partie d’une équipe engagée à créer un impact positif tangible sur nos communautés tout en relevant des défis stimulants et porteurs de sens. 
 Norda Stelo signifie étoile du Nord, là où les possibilités sont infinies en termes d’innovation, de développement et d’engagement.
 Notre vision est collective et notre ADN sérieusement humain!
 Ensemble, façonnons un avenir plus vert, plus durable et agissons auprès de nos clients pour les aider à faire face aux enjeux climatiques et environnementaux.
 Rejoignez Norda Stelo et Faites la Différence.
 L’équipe derrière le génie
 Le centre d’excellence Environnement, Changement Climatique et Communauté (E3C) de Norda Stelo est engagé dans la promotion d’un environnement favorable pour tous et accompagne ainsi ses clients dans le développement de leurs projets en veillant à la bonne intégration de ceux-ci dans leurs milieux. Les experts multidisciplinaires en environnement de Norda Stelo sont des pionniers bénéficiant de plusieurs décennies d’expertise dans la résolution de défis environnementaux complexes. Les enjeux liés à la protection de l’environnement ont toujours été une préoccupation majeure de Norda Stelo et cet engagement envers un environnement durable se reflète dans la diversité de ses services spécialisés. Norda Stelo s’engage ainsi à offrir des solutions innovantes et durables à ses clients aux prises avec des enjeux environnementaux complexes et interdépendants, pour faire face aux défis posés par les enjeux climatiques, contribuant à créer un avenir plus vert et plus sûr pour la communauté.
 Votre mandat
 Relevant du responsable de projet, la personne titulaire du poste agit comme appui professionnel dans l'exécution des projets majeurs d'évaluation des impacts environnementaux et sociaux (EIES) du CE-E3C, de la planification jusqu'au dépôt des livrables
 Vos défis
 Planification et suivi: Forte d'une excellente connaissance du processus d'EIES, elle planifie la réalisation de l'EIES et des études complémentaires et établit les échéanciers en tenant compte des dépendances entre les études et des contraintes d'inventaires. Elle organise et anime les rencontres de planification et assure le suivi auprès des équipes techniques et des sous-traitants afin de garantir le respect des calendriers.
 Qualité et cohérence des livrables. Elle effectue une relecture critique des études complémentaires et de l'EIES : elle vérifie que les études répondent à la directive, que leurs résultats sont fidèlement intégrés à l'EIES, que les figures, cartes et données soutiennent les interprétations qui en sont faites et que l'argumentaire est présenté de façon adaptée aux attentes des autorités. Elle formule des commentaires de révision aux experts et en assure le suivi jusqu'à leur intégration. Pour les questions d'expertise complexe, elle est appuyée par un professionnel senior en environnement.
 Suivi de projet. Elle participe enfin au suivi de l'avancement et de la performance des projets (budget, facturation, rapports d'avancement) dans SGP.
 Votre profil
 Baccalauréat en environnement, biologie, géographie, aménagement du territoire ou domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente jugée pertinente (l'expérience pertinente doit équivaloir à au moins 10 années de préparation de rapport d'études d'impact environnementale)
 Expérience significative en évaluation environnementale, dont une participation directe à plusieurs EIES complètes de projets majeurs (minier, portuaire, infrastructures linéaires ou industriels)
 •Expérience en coordination de livrables multidisciplinaires
 •Expérience de travail dans une firme de génie-conseil et ses exigences
 Maîtrise de la procédure québécoise d'évaluation et d'examen des impacts sur l'environnement (avis de projet, directive, étude d'impact, questions et commentaires, recevabilité, BAPE, décret)
 •Connaissance du processus fédéral (Loi sur l'évaluation d'impact, Agence d'évaluation d'impact du Canada)
 •Compréhension du contenu attendu d'une EIES : description du milieu, évaluation des impacts, mesures d'atténuation, effets cumulatifs, programmes de surveillance et de suivi
 Lecture critique des études complémentaires (faune, flore, milieu humain, milieu physique, etc.) et vérification de leur conformité à la directive
 •Capacité à repérer les incohérences entre les études, les données, les figures, les cartes et les conclusions
 •Jugement sur la stratégie de présentation : structure de l'argumentaire et anticipation des questions des autorités
 •Capacité à formuler des commentaires de révision constructifs à des experts plus spécialisés et à les faire cheminer jusqu'à la correction
 Élaboration et suivi d'échéanciers multidisciplinaires, incluant les dépendances entre les études et les contraintes des inventaires saisonniers
 •Organisation et animation de rencontres de planification et de suivi
 •Suivi des équipes techniques et des sous-traitants, et gestion des écarts
 •Suivi de l'avancement et de la performance financière des projets dans SGP ou un outil équivalent
 Rigueur, autonomie et sens de l'organisation
 •Aisance à remettre en question le travail d'experts de façon respectueuse
 •Excellente maîtrise du français écrit
 Bienvenue dans l'univers de Norda Stelo
 En rejoignant Norda Stelo, vous ferez partie d'une entreprise qui valorise l'innovation, le développement professionnel et la durabilité des actifs, qu’ils soient gris ou verts. Nous offrons un environnement de travail stimulant, des opportunités de croissance professionnelle et des avantages compétitifs. Vous aurez l'occasion de contribuer à des projets d'envergure dans des domaines variés à travers le monde.
 Qualité de vie et culture humaine : Profitez d’un équilibre vie professionnelle/vie personnelle grâce à des avantages tels que le télétravail, des horaires flexibles (congés le vendredi après-midi), un plan d’assurance collectif adapté, et des activités sociales stimulantes. En tant qu’entreprise certifiée B Corp et parmi les mieux gérées au Canada, Norda Stelo place le bien-être de ses employés au cœur de ses priorités. 
 Innovation et impact environnemental : Rejoignez une équipe dynamique et collaborative qui valorise la créativité pour relever les défis environnementaux. Chaque projet auquel vous participerez visera à créer des solutions durables ayant un impact positif sur la planète. 
 Engagement en développement durable : Contribuez activement à une vision commune d’un avenir respectueux de l’environnement en participant à des projets alignés avec des objectifs ambitieux de protection environnementale. 
 Développement professionnel : Profitez d’un soutien constant pour votre croissance personnelle et professionnelle, incluant formation continue, mentorat, et ressources pour développer vos compétences et évoluer dans votre carrière. 
 Collaborations interdisciplinaires : Travaillez aux côtés de professionnels issus de multiples disciplines (biologistes, géographes, géologues, urbanistes, etc.), enrichissant ainsi votre expérience grâce à une approche collaborative unique. 
 Ambiance collaborative et dynamique : Évoluez dans un environnement où votre expertise est valorisée et où les idées novatrices sont encouragées. Norda Stelo favorise une culture de travail positive, essentielle à l’innovation. 
Si vous êtes prêt(e) à relever de nouveaux défis et à contribuer à la protection de notre planète au sein d’une équipe passionnée et dynamique, nous sommes impatients de découvrir comment votre expertise peut enrichir notre équipe. 
Vous n’avez pas toute l’expérience souhaitée? Envisagez tout de même de postuler!
 Norda Stelo souscrit au principe d’accès à l’égalité en emploi et encourage fortement les femmes, les personnes issues de la diversité culturelle, les personnes en situation de handicap, les personnes appartenant aux communautés LGBTQIA2+, les personnes autochtones et/ou les personnes appartenant à un groupe traditionnellement marginalisé à poser leur candidature. 
 Nous pouvons offrir des mesures d’adaptation selon vos besoins. Pour plus de renseignements au sujet de notre milieu de travail accessible et de notre culture inclusive, veuillez nous contacter à l’adresse suivante : Talents@norda.com
